notes.title: Playtest starts
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45272246/f3f86c5755db17f676ad6f3a06381ef6b7a82c7e.jpg"][/img]
Follow Admiral Horatio Nelson to join the "Sea trials" of "The Weather Gage". You can add from now on the playtest version of this simulation to your Steam library. Thanks for your patience!

You will notice there is still really a lot of work to do, but as the Subanutica director explains in an interview as a goal for game-developers "You need to be embarrased with your first release ... if you are not embarrased by it you are probably waiting too long". Therefore your feedback is expected, that's the target of this playtest. You can provide feedback via the discussion group of the playtest [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/3479770"]Steam Community :: The Weather Gage Playtest[/url] (prefered) or using the function report within the game if you want to attach a picture (secondary: there are data limitations and is not visible to other testers who can provide more details on the same feedback)  In the same folder where the game is installed there is a manual as PDF. An in-game tutorial will have to wail until the gameplay mechanics are confirmed by this playtest and more mature.  [/p]

notes.title: Development status & next steps -December 2024
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45272246/ed7c4d05139c6924ad31a1c5210d28b7ce0ca57b.jpg[/img]

"The Weather Gage" is still under construction but getting ready for "sea trials" on Steam (i.e. playtesting)
In fact there is already ongoing playtesting. A first "virtual captain" with sailing experience and external to this project is testing the 4 most mature ships (merchant schooner, tartane, brig, 9pdr frigate). The feedback is overall positive, e.g. praising the feel and immersion of sailing (specially in first person view) or the level of detail of the frigate (biggest, most mature model). Quite positive too was that he could perform most common sailing manoeuvres such as wearing, tacking, heaving to or coming to anchor with the current controls and only a simple manual (a game tutorial will be included after more playtesting, when the current UI is validated). Also as a result of this playtesting came some improvements, most notably the new wind rose compass. You can see it on the game screenshot below (lower right corner) and you can see the difference if you compare with the "older" pictures on the store page (need to update).

Apart from working on improvements triggered by this first playtesting, the development focus is on the future Steam playtesting. First by integrating the Steam API on the original simulation (requirement to upload to Steam). In addition, now the simulation offers you the option to provide feedback, suggestions or bug findings within the programm, including a picture (i.e. no need to leave the simulation). The target is to make it easier for you to provide feedback during playtesting. You can see the buttons to take a picture and send the report at the bottom of the game screenshot below (these are temporary, will disappear in the finished simulation ;) ) .

The next step will be the  Steam Playtest signup possibility for you at the beginning of next year. There will be an announcement when you can start signing up.
